source.title: Anon: Extrapolating Adaptivity Beyond SGD and Adam
source.authors: Yi-Heng Zhang; Kai-Yan Zhao; Shao-Wu Wu; Yi-Ming Wang; Jia-Jun Wu; Leong Hou U; Steve Drew; Xiao-Guang Niu

record.tranche_reason: Compares optimizers on held-out or validation metrics across CNN, diffusion, and language modeling tasks; it uses different models, tasks, and metrics from the claim versions' original studies.
record.gate_note: The paper's citations to earlier optimizer comparisons are not rows. Included its own benchmark results and reported comparator metrics; the image-classification baselines in Tables 2–3 are sourced from prior publications, while the diffusion results and the other stated controlled comparisons include the authors' own runs.
record.test_reason: The authors reproduce adaptive-versus-SGDM image-classification comparisons and run a controlled, three-seed CIFAR-10 benchmark. These own results bear on V4. Cited ImageNet results and adaptive-versus-adaptive language-model comparisons do not independently test V4.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase is broadly accurate: the authors conclude that task-dependent adaptivity extrapolation and IDU make Anon a competitive element-wise optimizer, favoring negative adaptivity for CNNs and adaptivity at or above one for diffusion and Transformers. Their claim that Anon has the lowest loss on both GPT2 sizes is contradicted by Table 5: Sophia-G beats Anon on GPT2-medium.
record.recipe_differences: The study introduces and evaluates Anon, an optimizer with adaptivity extrapolation and Incremental Delay Update. CNN baseline metrics in Tables 2–3 are largely sourced from prior papers; the authors report controlled comparisons for diffusion and language modeling, plus a multi-seed CIFAR-10 benchmark.
record.method_sensitivity: Reported outcomes differ across task and architecture, and the selected γ and learning rate vary by task. The authors note that γ and learning rate are coupled; the diffusion search was not exhaustive.

fits_no_version.finding: Negative-adaptivity Anon exceeds SGDM on ImageNet and controlled CIFAR-10 CNN benchmarks.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A newly designed optimizer with searched negative adaptivity can outperform SGDM on these CNN benchmarks.

fits_no_version.finding: Anon improves diffusion FID over Adam and language-model validation loss over AdamW.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Changing the adaptive optimizer or its preconditioner can improve generation quality and language-model validation loss.

record.problems: The authors state that hyperparameter search was not exhaustive. ResNet50 Anon used a limited search; the 1B-parameter feasibility study was a single run. Many ResNet ImageNet comparator values are sourced from prior publications, rather than a common controlled run.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted from the reported task-level optimizer comparisons selected for V4. Table 5 time metrics, Tables 7–8 parameter similarity, and Tables 10, 12–13 IDU ablations were not extracted because they do not measure held-out optimizer performance against the V4 claim's named comparison.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and natural-label versus random-label held-out accuracy.
Convolutional versus fully connected architectures and local connectivity.

Equal-budget tuning restricted to learning rates and decay schedules; systematic broader tuning of the same optimizers; equal or better training performance despite worse held-out performance; Adam-to-SGD switching; isolated decoupled-weight-decay recovery; language-model comparisons against SGD.
Batch-size interventions under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
Magnitude-aware sharpness measurements and rankings of generalization gaps.

missing.what: Own-run AMSGradW accuracies: ResNet20 92.13 ± 0.10 and ResNet32 92.84 ± 0.19, compared with SGDM 92.33 ± 0.09 and 92.95 ± 0.04. These show smaller adaptive-method deficits than AdamW.

record.verdict_notes: Cited baseline numbers cannot support this study's independent verdicts. Appendix C.1 clarifies that SGDM and AdaBelief were reproduced, and AMSGradW was learning-rate-tuned. The controlled CIFAR benchmark reports standard deviations over three runs, not a formal significance test. No eligible result establishes a challenge to V4.

versions.untested_parts: Does not compare natural-label and random-label training or report memorization capacity.
No width sweep or interpolation-threshold analysis.
No convolutional versus fully connected architecture comparison.

Does not compare adaptive methods under the limited-tuning protocol described in the version, or test broad tuning as a systematic condition. Its optimizer and task coverage is partial; it reports CNN, diffusion, and language-model results.
Does not measure magnitude-aware sharpness or rank generalization gaps against norm- or margin-based measures.

rows.subject: SGDM
rows.operation_detail: ImageNet image classification; top-1 accuracy reported from reproduced/source baseline results.
rows.note: Reference comparator for the other Table 2 optimizer results.
rows.check: Valid comparator; Appendix C.1 explicitly identifies SGDM as reproduced by the authors. Its accuracy alone cannot establish the effect. The subject is an optimizer used with ResNet18.

rows.subject: Adam
rows.operation_detail: ImageNet image classification; top-1 accuracy reported from cited baseline results.
rows.note: Lower than the SGDM comparator.
rows.check: Cited Adam result from Liu et al. (2019), not this study's own result; exclude as independent evidence.

rows.subject: AMSGradW
rows.operation_detail: ImageNet image classification; AMSGrad with decoupled weight decay.
rows.note: The table defines AMSGradW as AMSGrad with decoupled weight decay.
rows.check: Authors' AMSGradW run, with learning rate searched over three values, reaches 68.78% versus reproduced SGDM's 69.94%. This supports the held-out-performance comparison; training-performance parity is not established.

rows.subject: AdaBelief
rows.operation_detail: ImageNet image classification; top-1 accuracy reported from cited baseline results.
rows.note: Slightly below the SGDM comparator.
rows.check: Appendix C.1 identifies AdaBelief as reproduced, rather than merely cited. Its 69.42% is 0.52 percentage points below SGDM, a smaller deficit than AMSGradW's.

source_check.correct: state=observed: AdaBelief reaches 69.42% versus SGDM's 69.94%, agreeing with V4's directional prediction. Appendix C.1 identifies AdaBelief as reproduced using recommended hyperparameters, correcting the operation's cited-baseline description.
source_check.problem: A smaller deficit alone does not establish incomplete realization of V4, which specifies no minimum performance gap.

rows.subject: AdaBound
rows.operation_detail: ImageNet image classification; top-1 accuracy reported from cited baseline results.
rows.note: Table marks this metric as cited from Luo et al. (2019).
rows.check: Cited AdaBound result from Luo et al. (2019); exclude as independent evidence.

rows.subject: Yogi

rows.subject: Anon
rows.operation_detail: ImageNet image classification with γ = −0.1; top-1 accuracy.
rows.note: Anon exceeds the SGDM reference; the paper associates this setting with negative adaptivity.
rows.check: Benchmark of the proposed optimizer after searching an additional adaptivity parameter. This does not establish reversal of V4's limited-tuning comparison or isolate a broader-tuning intervention on the same optimizer.

rows.subject: SGDM
rows.operation_detail: ImageNet image classification; top-1 accuracy from the authors' reproduced baseline.
rows.note: Reference comparator for the other Table 3 optimizer results.
rows.check: Valid reproduced SGDM comparator, but no independently eligible adaptive-versus-SGDM comparison among the extracted ResNet50 rows.

rows.subject: Adam
rows.operation_detail: ImageNet image classification; top-1 accuracy reported from cited baseline results.
rows.note: Table marks this metric as cited from Xie et al. (2022).
rows.check: Cited Adam result from Xie et al. (2022); exclude as independent evidence.

rows.subject: Anon
rows.operation_detail: ImageNet image classification with η = 1 and γ = −0.1; top-1 accuracy.
rows.note: The paper states the Anon search was limited and reports γ = −0.1.
rows.check: Performance of the proposed negative-adaptivity optimizer is a method benchmark, not a reversal of the specified limited-tuning Adam-class comparison.

rows.subject: Adam
rows.operation_detail: CIFAR-10 diffusion-model training; FID reported.
rows.note: The table compares five optimizer configurations.
rows.check: Diffusion-generation FID is outside V4's image-classification and language benchmarks. The text also inconsistently names AdamW in the search description and Adam in Table 4.

rows.subject: Anon
rows.operation_detail: CIFAR-10 diffusion-model training with γ = 1; FID reported.
rows.note: Authors say γ = 1 differs from Adam only by IDU.
rows.check: Proposed-method diffusion benchmark against Adam; neither the task nor the optimizer contrast establishes V4.

rows.subject: Anon

rows.note: The paper calls this highly competitive and reports the setting as slightly extrapolated adaptivity.
rows.check: Proposed-method diffusion benchmark against Adam; lower FID is not reversal of an adaptive-versus-SGD generalization deficit.

rows.subject: AdamW
rows.operation_detail: OpenWebText language modeling; validation loss and time reported.
rows.note: Reference comparator for Anon and Sophia-G.

rows.subject: Anon
rows.operation_detail: OpenWebText language modeling with γ = 1.1; validation loss and time reported.
rows.note: Anon has lower validation loss than AdamW.
rows.check: Anon versus AdamW compares two adaptive methods, without SGD. The claimed lowest loss applies to GPT2-small but not GPT2-medium.

rows.subject: AdamW

rows.subject: Anon
rows.operation_detail: OpenWebText language modeling with γ = 1; validation loss and time reported.
rows.note: Anon has lower validation loss than AdamW.
rows.check: Anon versus AdamW does not test V4's contrast. Anon improves over AdamW, but Sophia-G has lower loss still: 2.70653 versus 2.69017 for Anon.
